hooks.command: input=$(cat); export CLAUDE_SESSION_ID=$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.session_id // empty'); printf '%s' "$input" | node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-$HOME/.claude/plugins/cache/ecc/ecc/2.2.0}/scripts/hooks/session-activity-tracker.js" 2>/dev/null || true

PostToolUse.description: Real, per-tool-call usage log to ~/.claude/metrics/tool-usage.jsonl -- best-effort, needs ECC installed in this session (attach ECC-aesop) to actually record.

hooks.prompt:
The user has the ECC plugin's git-workflow, github-ops, code-reviewer, security-reviewer, orch-add-feature, and hookify skills/agents available. Here is a Bash tool call that just ran: $ARGUMENTS

Only flag if the command is git commit / git push / gh pr create|merge / gh api on branch-protection or repo settings, AND there is no sign in the command or its context that a review or CI check already happened (e.g. it is not going through an already-set-up PR+CI+auto-merge flow). If it's a routine read-only git/gh command (status, log, diff, fetch, api GET), or part of an already-established PR flow, respond OK. Otherwise respond with a one-line flag naming which skill/agent should have been used instead and why.

PostToolUse.description: Flags (does not block) Bash git/GitHub commands that look like unreviewed raw work bypassing an available ECC skill/agent.
